description:
About the Position

Cranfield University is offering an EPSRC-supported doctorate on how legumes affect nitrogen availability in regenerative arable rotations.

The research connects soil processes with crop performance and greenhouse-gas mitigation.

Official Project Title

Understanding legume nitrogen dynamics and their implications for greenhouse gas mitigation in regenerative agriculture

Research Focus and Methods

Combine field, laboratory and controlled-environment experiments to quantify nitrogen fixation, mineralisation, crop uptake and emissions. Compare detailed nitrogen accounting with conventional tests and investigate fertiliser-replacement potential.

Research Training and Development

A Dundee placement with the James Hutton Institute connects the project with long-term cropping trials.

Funding and Duration

Studentship funding and award conditions
ComponentDetails
AwardPhD studentship; selection is competitive
ProgrammeEPSRC Doctoral Landscape Award
DurationThree years full-time
StipendAdvertised annual tax-free bursary up to £24,500 for three years.
Tuition and research supportEPSRC/Cranfield fee support and stipend. The advert explicitly quantifies Home-fee coverage; Overseas applicants should confirm their full fee award.
Award conditionsSelection is competitive; an advertised project does not guarantee a studentship.
Stipend amount statusThe advert publishes a bursary of up to £24,500 annually. This maximum is not confirmation of an individual award amount.

Eligibility and English Language

Applicant qualifications and funding eligibility
ComponentDetails
Applicant eligibilityHome and Overseas applicants may apply, but Overseas-funded places are limited.
Academic preparationFirst- or second-class UK honours degree or equivalent in a relevant field such as soil/environmental science, agronomy, plant science or ecology.
Project interests and skillsInterest in fieldwork, laboratory analysis and quantitative methods such as R; training is provided.
English languageMeet the host university’s English-language admission rules. An approved alternative or exemption may apply; IELTS is not universally mandatory.

Cranfield University is a specialist postgraduate university in England focused on technology and management.
